current.text: Yahoo lists him as questionable for rest.
Phoenix says Jalen Green is the point guard. The team wants to reduce Booker's ballhandling load and make spacing easier for him.
Josh still expects Booker to be the de facto point guard with about 32% usage. That should keep his assists good.
He starts next to Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges. These four are expected to take most of Phoenix's minutes and usage.
Experts expect Jalen Green and Miles Bridges to take touches from him.
Experts do not expect a big bounce back. They project a season close to last year's finish, around 40th in categories, and doubt he is still a top 20 player.
Experts say his rank around 23 is too high and that he should not go in round one. They value him at about a round four pick. In an auction mock he went for 22 USD, and Josh called that a good price.

durable.text: He is an elite free throw shooter on high volume, about 7 to 8 attempts per game, so he lifts a team's FT% clearly.
Josh notes that even a shooter at about 89% from the line could have a random drop to around 81% in a season.
Points are a league outlier strength, and he also gives good assists for a guard.
Turnovers are his weak category, at about 3 per game. That is high even for a guard.
Josh calls his FG% weak and says he does not give enough threes, steals or blocks.
Ben calls him an average defender. He is not a net negative, but he is not a good defender either.

tags.name: sites disagree on price
tags.detail: Yahoo value 31 USD, ESPN value 17 USD

note: He cost 45 USD in our league last season. The Yahoo value is 31 USD and the ESPN value is 17 USD, and the experts set his price around the low 20s USD (a mock went for 22 USD), so do not pay anything near last year's price. He is best in a punt TO build, where his points, FT% and assists count fully and his roughly 3 turnovers a game matter little. Early in the season, check whether he or Jalen Green runs the offense, since that drives his assists, and watch his rest status (Yahoo Q).
